In [[geometry]], the '''elongated pentagonal rotunda''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s (''J''<sub>21</sub>). As the name suggests, it can be constructed by elongating a [[pentagonal rotunda]] (''J''<sub>6</sub>) by attaching a [[decagonal prism]] to its base. It can also be seen as an [[elongated pentagonal orthobirotunda]] (''J''<sub>42</sub>) with one pentagonal rotunda removed.

{{Johnson solid}}
[[File:J21 elongated pentagonal rotunda.stl|thumb|3D model of an elongated pentagonal rotunda]]

==Formulae==
The following [[formula]]e for [[volume]] and [[surface area]] can be used if all [[face (geometry)|faces]] are [[regular polygon|regular]], with edge length ''a'':<ref>[[Stephen Wolfram]], "[https://www.wolframalpha.com/input/?i=Elongated+pentagonal+rotunda Elongated pentagonal rotunda]" from [[Wolfram Alpha]]. Retrieved July 22, 2010.</ref>

<math>V=\frac{1}{12}\left(45+17\sqrt{5}+30\sqrt{5+2\sqrt{5}}\right)a^3\approx14.612...a^3</math>

<math>A=\frac{1}{2}\left(20+\sqrt{5\left(145+58\sqrt{5}+2\sqrt{30\left(65+29\sqrt{5}\right)}\right)}\right)a^2\approx32.3472...a^2</math>

=== Dual polyhedron ===

The dual of the elongated pentagonal rotunda has 30 faces: 10 isosceles triangles, 10 rhombi, and 10 quadrilaterals.
